title: Double Check, Then the Rook
setup: Your rook and knight share the d-file with the black king — the knight in front, the check waiting behind it.
hint: One knight jump can check the king by itself and uncover the rook's check as well. Pick the jump that also hits something.
explanation:
## The Idea

{{Nc6+}} is a double check: the knight attacks d8 itself, and moving it uncovers the rook on d1 behind it. Against two checks at once neither a capture nor a block helps, so the king has to move. Wherever it goes, {{Nxb8}} collects the rook the knight was eyeing all along, and even if the king then takes the knight, your rook is left against a bare king. Double check is the most forcing move in chess: the king must move, and everything else waits.
